items.statement: Residents and assessors experience the EPA target mainly as a documentation quota, and this shapes which activities are requested and when forms are completed.
items.rationale: A working proposition to examine, not a hypothesis to test: it follows retrieved accounts (c1, c5) and matters for the June target decision; feasibility is high because the programme can reach all groups.
items.risks: Participants may repeat familiar complaints; negative cases must be sought.

items.statement: Assessors delay completion because the form is separated from the feedback conversation they value.
items.rationale: Suggested by assessor focus groups; would point to redesigning the form around the conversation.
items.risks: May be specific to assessors with heavy clinical loads.

items.statement: Struggling residents avoid requesting assessments, so the target hides the residents it should detect.
items.rationale: Chief residents reported this pattern; if it holds locally it matters for patient safety as well as for education.
items.risks: Hard to recruit the residents concerned.

summary: Three working propositions; h1 selected as the organising proposition, h2 and h3 as sensitising concepts.
